correctness.rationale: Unique integral parametrization M=t w(-v,u)^T for a canonical primitive kernel line, with c(M)=|t| and sup norm |t| height(w)^2. Primitive sector lattice counts have leading coefficient (12/pi^2) mu(I)x^2 and O_I(x log(2x)) error. Summation t<=T^alpha at radial cutoff qT gives (24/pi^2) alpha q mu(I)T logT plus controlled errors, normalized by the already known exact count 8 sum phi(m)floor(T/m^2). Endpoint alpha=1 follows by mass squeeze. Finite direct reconstruction checks 19 full boxes up to 50, 175 joint windows, and 299 independent content-sum identities; finite checks do not prove the limit.

originality.rationale: The *joint independence and explicit projective kernel density*, not the known total count, are the assessed claim. The October 2026 prescribed-characteristic-polynomial paper gives general upper bounds. The 2008 fixed-eigenvalue paper counts a broader family and bounds the repeated-eigenvalue locus. OEIS A211422 and A120486 directly cover the unrefined count and asymptotic; this coverage is stated, and those known facts are excluded from novelty. Searches of related published records and accessible own claims did not show this refined joint law. General equidistribution technology remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The statistics are intrinsic and motivated: entry gcd measures arithmetic content, scaled matrix norm measures radial placement in the sampling box, and kernel slope measures projective direction on the singular nilpotent variety. The explicit three-way asymptotic independence and heavy-tailed direction density resolve a natural distributional question not determined by the long-known total counting sequence, giving restricted asymptotics at any fixed arithmetic content exponent, radial cutoff, and angular window. This is a structural result for a natural characteristic-polynomial stratum, not an arbitrary finite computation.
